OH radical scavenging function

Source: R/scavenge_oh.R
scavenge_oh.Rd

The background hydroxyl radical scavenging term is a measure of the degradation rate of non-target constituents in a water. The term is defined as the sum of the reaction rate of the constituent multiplied by the concentration of the constituent: sum(k_i * [C]i) where k_i is the reaction rate of a contaminant and [C]i its concentration. Supporting Information in Wang et al. 2019 provides the definition and additional methods for calculating background scavenging. For a data frame of waters, use scavenge_oh_df, which adds the scavenging term as a new column.

Usage

scavenge_oh(water, dose = 0, kdoc_adjust = 25000)

scavenge_oh_df(
  df,
  input_water = "defined",
  output_column = "oh_scavenging",
  dose = "use_col",
  kdoc_adjust = "use_col"
)

Source

See references list at: https://github.com/BrownandCaldwell-Public/tidywater/wiki/References

Brezonik and Fulkerson-Brekken (1998)

Buxton et al. (1988)

Coddington et al. (1999)

Katsoyiannis et al. (2011)

Larson and Zepp (1988)

Vinge et al. (2020)

Vinge et al. (2021)

Wang et al. (2019)

Wols and Hofman-Caris (2012)

Wols et al. (2014)

Arguments

water

Source water of tidywater 'water' object type

dose

Hydrogen peroxide (h2o2) dose applied in mg/L, defaults to 0

kdoc_adjust

Optional input for a different k_DOC rate constant for fitting data, defaults to 2.5e4 L/mg C/s. See Details for other reported values.

df

a data frame containing a water class column, which has already been computed using define_water_df. The df may include columns named for the H2O2 dose in mg/L and the DOC rate constant.

input_water

name of the column of water class data to be used as the input. Default is "defined".

output_column

name of the output column storing the OH radical scavenging term in s^-1. Default is "oh_scavenging".

Value

scavenge_oh returns the total background hydroxyl radical scavenging term in units of s^-1.

scavenge_oh_df returns a data frame containing the original data frame and a column with the background hydroxyl radical scavenging term in s^-1.

Details

Rate constants used in the code:

  • DOC: 2.5e4 L/mg C/s (Larson and Zepp 1988; 3.0e8 M_C^-1 s^-1 divided by 12,011 mg C/mol)

  • HCO3-: 8.5e6 M^-1 s^-1 (Buxton et al. 1988)

  • CO3 2-: 3.9e8 M^-1 s^-1 (Buxton et al. 1988)

  • NO2-: 1.0e10 M^-1 s^-1 (Coddington et al. 1999; Vinge et al. 2020)

  • NO3-: 1.0e5 M^-1 s^-1 (Buxton et al. 1988)

  • H2O2: 2.7e7 M^-1 s^-1 (Buxton et al. 1988)

Other reported DOC rate constants, for use as kdoc_adjust. Sources report these per mole of carbon (M_C^-1 s^-1); they are converted to L/mg C/s by dividing by 12,011 mg C/mol. Brezonik and Katsoyiannis values are as compiled in Wols and Hofman-Caris (2012), Table 2.

  • 2.41e4 (2.9e8 M_C^-1 s^-1): lake and river water, Brezonik and Fulkerson-Brekken (1998)

  • 2.25e4 (2.7e8 M_C^-1 s^-1): Lake Zurich, Katsoyiannis et al. (2011)

  • 1.67e4 (2.0e8 M_C^-1 s^-1): Lake Jonsvatnet, Katsoyiannis et al. (2011)

  • 1.75e4 (2.1e8 M_C^-1 s^-1): Lake Greifensee, Katsoyiannis et al. (2011)

  • 2.91e4 (3.5e8 M_C^-1 s^-1): effluent organic matter, Katsoyiannis et al. (2011)

  • 1.67e4 (2.0e8 M_C^-1 s^-1): model value, Wols et al. (2014), Table 3

  • 5.29e4 (6.35e8 M_C^-1 s^-1): midpoint of the 3.5e8 to 9.2e8 range cited by Vinge et al. (2021)

Examples

water1 <- define_water(ph=7, doc=3, alk = 70, no3 = 4)
#> Warning: Missing value for `toc`; DOC assumed to be 95% of TOC.
#> Warning: Major ions, TDS, and conductivity are all missing; assuming ideal conditions.
#> Ionic strength will be "NA" and activity coefficients will be 1.
h2o2_dose<-20

background_scavenging <- scavenge_oh(water1, h2o2_dose)

background_SC_adjusted <- scavenge_oh(water1, h2o2_dose, 1.67e4) # Katsoyiannis et al. (2011)


example_df <- water_df %>%
  define_water_df() %>%
  scavenge_oh_df(dose = 10)

example_df <- water_df %>%
  define_water_df() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(h2o2 = seq(2, 24, 2)) %>%
  scavenge_oh_df(dose = h2o2, kdoc_adjust = 1.67e4, output_column = "sc")
